doc_verification.detail: Reachability: WebFetch was domain_blocked for api.qdrant.tech, but the page was fetched successfully via the web-reader fallback (title 'Update collection aliases | Qdrant | API Reference') -> PASS. Version: URL path v-1-18-x and page selector 'v1.18.x' match target v1.18.0 -> PASS. Content: the RENDERED page prose says only 'Updates aliases for the specified collections.' and never uses the word 'atomic'; the contract's [SPEC description] wording exists verbatim in the OpenAPI spec the reference is generated from — bundled in the v1.18.0 clone at docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json:11093: 'Alias changes are atomic, meaning that no collection modifications can happen between alias operations.' — but that sentence defines atomicity as ISOLATION (no interleaved collection modifications), not literally all-or-nothing rollback on failure; the contract assertion additionally claims 'no intermediate state is observable', whose failure-path reading the observation contradicts -> PARTIAL. Endpoint: registry entry aliases+update (structured_contract.json:3879-3930) — POST /collections/aliases, required body actions array of create_alias/delete_alias/rename_alias, query timeout>=1, response result:boolean — all match the observed traffic (positive 200 {"result":true,...}; negative 404 error envelope) -> PASS.

http_semantics.note: The invalid batch was NOT swallowed into a 2xx — the target correctly returned 404 with a descriptive error naming the missing collection. The violation is purely post-rejection state consistency: the first action of the rejected batch remained applied. No illegal-2xx dimension in this chain.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: alias operations in one request are applied atomically - no intermediate state is observable and no collection modification can interleave
contract_grounding.note: Violates-declaration self-check: the observed phenomenon (alias persisted and observable via GET /aliases after the batch was rejected 404) lies squarely inside the assertion's constraint domain — same endpoint, same actions list, and it is precisely an observable non-final state after a non-atomic partial application; violates=true is not conservative drift. Contract description field (for context): 'alias changes are ATOMIC: no collection modifications can happen between the alias operations of one request [SPEC description]'. Interpretive tension for the auditor: the spec sentence's own definition of atomic is isolation-flavored; the violated clause is the assertion's added 'no intermediate state is observable'.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:180 #[post("/collections/aliases")] -> dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::ChangeAliases) -> lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:82 route arm -> update_aliases (line 299). update_aliases takes both locks then iterates operation.actions SEQUENTIALLY: for create_alias it first validates (collections_ops.rs:25 validate_collection_exists — the exact source of the observed 404 text 'Collection `X` doesn't exist!') and then calls alias_lock.insert, which (alias_mapping.rs:66-70) mutates the in-memory HashMap AND durably saves data.json PER ACTION. The `?` operator early-returns on the first failing action with NO rollback of already-persisted actions. Mechanism matches all observations: valid-first batch -> action 1 persisted, action 2 fails 404 -> leaked create; delete-first destructive batch -> alias removed+saved, then create fails -> leaked delete; invalid-first batch -> fails before any mutation -> clean. The gRPC face (src/tonic/api/collections_api.rs:124 update_aliases -> ChangeAliases) funnels into the same meta-op, so the behavior is face-shared by construction; a behavioral REST-vs-gRPC differential was not run in this sandbox (single-face observation) and is not fabricated.
source_grounding.outcome_note: Per-action validation IS present (the batch was correctly rejected with 404 and a precise error). What is absent is batch-level all-or-nothing application: no staging of the batch, no end-of-batch single persist, no rollback on mid-batch failure — only lock-based isolation plus eager per-op persistence in a sequential loop. NOT marked by_design_in_source: the only in-code intent comments assert atomicity rather than disclaim it — collection_meta_ops.rs:298 'performs several alias changes in an atomic fashion' and line 304 'Prevent search on partially switched collections' (lock rationale); no comment, docstring, or maintainer citation anywhere in lib/storage/src declares failure-path partial application intended (grep rollback|all-or.nothing|by design|intentionally returned no disclaimers).

excluded: env: positive control returned 200 and applied both aliases; service answered every request; rejection semantics were correct

concurrency: scripts are strictly sequential with unique ownership prefixes (bau8/sau1/s2au2); three independent runs at different times reproduce identically; the code path holds both write locks for the whole loop, so interleaving cannot explain the leaked state

cache_delay: post-rejection state was read back via fresh GET /aliases 200 responses (sibling logs carry the full response bodies showing the leaked alias present and, in the destructive case, the pre-existing alias gone)
request_typo: the missing-collection name is intentional; the 404 error text names the exact queried collection
mundane_explanation.surviving: Interpretive question only (auditor scope): whether the spec's isolation-flavored 'atomic' wording ('no collection modifications can happen between alias operations') contractually promises all-or-nothing rollback on batch failure; under the contract assertion's own clause 'no intermediate state is observable', the observed post-404 partial state violates. Source shows rollback was never implemented — only lock isolation.
